tagline: Out of a village the fires made small, near Boone's old station.
intro: North Cleveland Road, KY 1973, leaves the village of Athens at the Athens-Boonesboro Road and runs north for about six miles through rural eastern Fayette County to US 60, the Winchester Road.

Athens, said locally as AY-thenz, began as Cross Plains. Early on it had a woolen factory and a bagging and rope works, and fire had taken all of them by 1860. In 1853 and 1854 a single blaze swept away every business house on the south side of Main Street west of the Cleveland pike, and the fires left the village's business center the size it is now.

moments.title: Athens
moments.text: At the corner of Main Street and Cleveland Road stands the Aubrey Inn of about 1800, one of the old village buildings, most of them homes now, in a National Register district.

moments.title: Boone Station
moments.text: Daniel Boone made his home at this frontier station on Boone's Creek from 1779 to 1782, until the tangle of Kentucky land claims cost him the ground.
